subject: Neurology
vignette: A researcher stains a section of cerebral cortex with Nissl stain to identify neuronal somata. She observes intense staining of some neuronal processes but a complete absence of staining in the long output processes of the same neurons.
question: Which neuronal structure will FAIL to be visualized by Nissl staining?

options.text: Rough ER of a large motor neuron soma

explanation_correct: Nissl stain binds rough endoplasmic reticulum, which is abundant in neuronal soma and dendrites but absent from axons. Axons therefore appear unstained, a property useful for distinguishing them from dendrites on histology. Neurons can also be identified with markers such as neurofilament protein and synaptophysin.

explanation_incorrect.A: The soma contains abundant rough ER (Nissl bodies) and stains intensely.
explanation_incorrect.C: Dendrites contain rough ER and are visualized with Nissl stain, unlike axons.
explanation_incorrect.D: Nissl bodies are exactly the clusters of rough ER that this stain highlights.
explanation_incorrect.E: Large motor neuron somata are especially rich in rough ER and stain strongly.

educationalObjective: Nissl stain demonstrates rough ER in soma and dendrites but not in axons.

subject: Neurology
vignette: An embryology researcher is tracing the lineages of the various support cells of the nervous system. She finds that most CNS glial cells share a neuroectodermal origin, while one CNS cell type arises from mesoderm and the PNS glia arise from neural crest.
question: Which of the following CNS cells is derived from a different embryonic germ layer than the other CNS glia?
explanation_correct: Microglia are specialized macrophages derived from mesoderm, unlike the other CNS glia (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells), which arise from neuroectoderm. PNS glia, including Schwann cells and satellite cells, derive from neural crest ectoderm. Microglia serve as the phagocytic scavengers of the CNS and fuse into multinucleated giant cells in HIV-associated dementia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Astrocytes are CNS glia of neuroectodermal origin, not mesodermal.
explanation_incorrect.B: Oligodendrocytes derive from neuroectoderm, like other CNS glia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ependymal cells are neuroectodermally derived CNS glia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Choroid plexus is a specialized ependymal derivative and is neuroectodermal.

educationalObjective: Microglia are mesoderm-derived; all other CNS glia are neuroectoderm-derived and PNS glia are neural crest-derived.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient sustains a CNS injury and subsequently shows prominent reactive gliosis at the lesion site. Immunohistochemistry highlights a GFAP-positive cell that provides physical support, helps clear excess neurotransmitters, and contributes to the blood-brain barrier.
question: Which glial cell is GFAP-positive, is the largest and most abundant in the CNS, and serves as a glycogen fuel reserve buffer?
explanation_correct: Astrocytes are the largest and most abundant glial cells in the CNS and are GFAP-positive. They provide physical support and repair (reactive gliosis), remove excess neurotransmitters, form part of the blood-brain barrier via their foot processes, and store glycogen as a fuel reserve buffer. These functions make them central to CNS homeostasis and injury response.

explanation_incorrect.B: Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons and are not the GFAP-positive support cell described.
explanation_incorrect.C: Microglia are phagocytic cells of mesodermal origin and are not GFAP-positive.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ependymal cells are ciliated columnar cells that line ventricles, not the support cell described.
explanation_incorrect.E: Schwann cells are PNS glia that myelinate a single axon and are S100-positive.

educationalObjective: Astrocytes are the abundant GFAP-positive CNS glia that support repair, neurotransmitter clearance, the BBB, and glycogen storage.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has relapsing-remitting neurologic deficits and MRI plaques in the CNS white matter. Histologic examination of a demyelinated plaque shows cells with a 'fried egg' appearance, and the patient's optic nerve (CN II) is also affected.
question: Which glial cell is injured in this disease, myelinates CNS axons including CN II, and myelinates approximately 30 axons per cell?
explanation_correct: Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons, including the optic nerve (CN II), have a characteristic 'fried egg' histologic appearance, and each myelinates many axons (about 30). They are the predominant glial cell of white matter and are injured in multiple sclerosis, leukodystrophies, and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. In contrast, Schwann cells myelinate a single PNS axon and are S100-positive.

explanation_incorrect.A: Schwann cells myelinate the PNS (CN III-XII), one axon each, and are injured in Guillain-Barre syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.B: Astrocytes provide support and form the blood-brain barrier but do not myelinate axons.
explanation_incorrect.D: Microglia are phagocytic scavengers, not myelin-producing cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Satellite cells surround neuronal somata in PNS ganglia and do not myelinate CNS axons.

educationalObjective: Oligodendrocytes myelinate many CNS axons (including CN II) and are damaged in multiple sclerosis.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A histology section shows a ciliated simple columnar layer lining the ventricles, whose apical cilia circulate CSF and whose microvilli aid CSF absorption. In a separate HIV-positive patient, phagocytic cells in the CNS fuse to form multinucleated giant cells.
question: Which cell type lines the ventricles and central canal and, in a specialized form (choroid plexus), produces CSF?
explanation_correct: Ependymal cells are ciliated simple columnar glial cells that line the ventricles and the central canal of the spinal cord. Their apical cilia circulate CSF, microvilli assist absorption, and specialized choroid plexus ependymal cells produce CSF. The multinucleated giant cells mentioned in the vignette are fused HIV-infected microglia, a distinct phagocytic cell type.

explanation_incorrect.A: Microglia are phagocytes that fuse in HIV dementia but do not line ventricles or produce CSF.
explanation_incorrect.B: Astrocytes support the BBB and repair but do not form the ciliated ventricular lining.
explanation_incorrect.C: Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons and are not involved in CSF production.
explanation_incorrect.D: Schwann cells are PNS myelin cells and are not present lining CNS ventricles.

educationalObjective: Ependymal cells line ventricles/central canal and form choroid plexus, which produces CSF.
